target.detail: the side return, gate on the latch

setup: Side gate on the latch, recycling not taken in, three days of post fanning under the letterbox. Nobody home and the house knows it.
on_success: Patio door lifts off the runner like it was asking. In, sweep the usual drawers, out before the security light even decides.
on_fail: Motion light, then a dog you didn't hear about, then a neighbour at their window in a dressing gown filming you. Three strikes in four seconds.
on_crit: Jewellery box under the socks, exactly where everyone hides it, exactly why everyone looks there. Somebody's nan's gold, and now it's yours.

target.detail: the one lit window on a dark street

setup: Whole terrace dark except one — telly flicker upstairs, keys and a watch on the hall table you can see through the glass.
on_success: Letterbox, fishing rod, keys off the table. You never even open a window. They rebooked the whole street's trust for this.
on_fail: The telly-flicker was a plug timer. Real them was in the kitchen the whole time and now they're between you and the door.
on_crit: Car keys too. There's a nice German thing on the drive and you've suddenly got a way home.

setup: Half-done loft conversion, scaffold up the front, first-floor window on the latch because the builders can't be bothered either.
on_success: Up the boards, in the window, out with the tools and whatever the owners left in the 'safe' room. The builders get blamed. Everyone wins except them.
on_fail: Scaffold board was loose and so was your footing. You come down the quick way, ankle first, into the skip.
on_crit: They'd moved the good stuff up here to keep it from the builders. Kept it lovely for you instead.

target.detail: the one with the dog bowl by the back step

setup: Full bowl of water on the step, no dog barking. Either it's out with them or it's the quiet kind that waits. The kitchen window's on the latch either way.
on_success: In and out through the kitchen. The dog watches from a basket and decides you're not worth the effort. Sensible dog.
on_fail: Not the quiet kind. It comes round the side of the house already committed and you leave a trainer behind.

target.name: Priya
target.detail: top-floor flat, scaffolding up the front all month

setup: Refurb job, scaffold to the third floor, boards wet from the afternoon. One window without a sticker on it, which means one flat the alarm firm didn't finish.
on_success: Up the boards, in the unstickered window, out the same way with a laptop and a jar of pound coins somebody was saving for something.
on_fail: The board you trusted wasn't clipped in. You come down faster than you went up and land in the skip, which is the only lucky part.
on_crit: Whoever lives here doesn't trust banks. You find out exactly how much in a shoebox on top of the wardrobe.

target.detail: keys you can see on the hall table through the glass

setup: Bungalow, single glazing, and a set of keys on the hall table catching the streetlight. There's a car on the drive those keys almost certainly open.
on_success: Letterbox, a length of wire, patience. Keys off the table without touching the door. The car's yours before they've turned over in bed.
on_fail: The wire slips and the keys go on the floor with a sound the whole quiet street can hear. A landing light comes on upstairs.
on_crit: House keys, car keys, and a fob for a lock-up you'll be looking into on Thursday.

target.detail: the house that's been empty since the funeral

setup: Curtains half-drawn the same way for six weeks, a wheelie bin nobody's put out, a small pile of condolence cards fanned under the letterbox that nobody's come to read.
on_success: A quiet house that doesn't fight you. You take the telly and the tools and leave the photographs, which is the one line you keep.
on_fail: A neighbour's been keeping an eye out of respect and there's nothing more dangerous than a respectful neighbour with a phone.

target.detail: the show home nobody actually lives in

setup: Estate half-built, one house done up perfect to sell the rest. Staged furniture, a fruit bowl that's plastic, and appliances still in the film they came wrapped in.
on_success: Everything's boxed-fresh and nothing's been registered. You clear the white goods into the van like a delivery running backwards.
on_fail: The show home's the one thing on site with a live alarm and a camera, because it's the one thing they're trying to sell.
on_crit: The sales office next door was never locked. There's a safe in it and a very bad four-digit code.

target.name: Aaron
target.detail: the shared house where nobody owns the front door

setup: Six locks on six bedroom doors and a communal hallway anyone can walk into. Bikes in the corridor, a whiteboard about the bins, and nobody who'd stop a stranger.
on_success: You walk in like you're viewing a room. One bedroom door's been left on the latch by a lad running for the bus. That's his lesson, not yours.
on_fail: Turns out one of them works nights and sleeps days, and you've just woken him up standing in his doorway.

target.detail: the ground-floor window somebody opened for the heat and forgot

setup: First proper warm day of the year and half the street's opened up. One window swung wide onto an empty front room, curtains breathing in and out with the wind.
on_success: You don't even climb in fully — arm through, bag off the sofa, handbag off the hook, gone before the curtain's finished its next breath.
on_fail: There's a baby asleep in that front room and a mum in the kitchen who hears the wrong kind of quiet.
